purpose: Sulindac is used to relieve pain, swelling, stiffness, and tenderness caused by conditions like arthritis, gout, and other inflammatory conditions. It helps you move more comfortably and feel better day to day. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other types of pain and inflammation.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain and swelling. Sulindac works by blocking the enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) that your body uses to make those chemicals. With fewer of those chemicals around, you experience less pain and inflammation.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, diarrhea, constipation, dizziness, and headache. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset. Some people may also notice swelling in their hands or feet.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of serious stomach bleeding, ulcers, heart attack, or stroke — especially if taken for a long time or at high doses. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, heart disease, or are pregnant. Avoid taking it with other NSAIDs like ibuprofen or naproxen. Do not take it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Older adults should use it with extra caution.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 150 mg to 200 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening) with food. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on your condition. Do not take more than 400 mg per day unless your doctor tells you to.
